subject: Buffered-burst pricing, rollover credits, and sustained-volume tiers
content:
From: Sam Levin <sam@gridpay.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing question: high burst and rollover credits

Hi Evelyn,

Quick question as we map our forecast for H2: we expect a sustained baseline of ~220M tokens/month, with predictable weekly peaks up to ~600M tokens (spikes during batch jobs). We are evaluating a hosted arrangement but want to understand how Redwood treats burst capacity relative to committed volume, and whether unused committed tokens can roll over month-to-month as credits.

Can you send the current tiered-rate options and any examples of rollover mechanics? Also curious if there is a path to a hybrid where some dedicated capacity is reserved for predictable peaks.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Levin
CTO, GridPay

---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Levin <sam@gridpay.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing question: high burst and rollover credits

Hi Sam — great framing, thanks. High-level options we typically propose for a profile like yours:

1) Sustained Commit + Buffered Burst add-on
   - Commit to a sustained monthly baseline (e.g., 200M tokens) at a discounted per-1M rate
   - Purchase a small buffered burst pool (prepaid tokens available for sudden peaks) priced between hosted and dedicated marginal rates
   - Unused committed tokens: option to roll over up to 25% of monthly commit for one month, or convert unused into credit toward additional burst pool purchases

2) Tiered Consumption Bands (no hard commit)
   - Volume breakpoints with step discounts as cumulative consumption crosses thresholds in a billing period
   - Better for unpredictable workloads but discounts accrue only after thresholds are reached

3) Hybrid Dedicated for Peak Windows
   - Small dedicated instance(s) reserved for scheduled batch peaks; hosted API handles baseline and ad hoc queries
   - Dedicated reservation provides guaranteed throughput and predictable latency but is priced higher; credits can be applied toward hosted consumption if dedicated capacity is unused during a billing window

Attached is a draft rate card and an example worksheet we can use to model GridPay numbers. Can Rishi and Lauren weigh in on the SLA/credit mechanics and recommended default band breakpoints?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rate_card_draft.pdf (18 KB), sample_rollover_model.xlsx (12 KB)

- For rollover, we would prefer a longer runway (we were hoping for up to 2 months carryover of unused committed tokens, capped at 50% of monthly commit), otherwise we risk overcommitting to avoid throttling costs.

If there is a simple LOI template, we can do an internal fast-track sign once we see an example pricing schedule.

Best,
Sam

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Levin <sam@gridpay.io>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing question: high burst and rollover credits

Sam — appreciate the usage snapshot. Based on that, here is a concise commercial proposal (attached as rate_card_v3.pdf):

Option A — Sustain Plus Burst (recommended)
- Commit: 200M tokens / month at $4.50 per 1M tokens (24% off list)
- Buffered burst pool: purchase in blocks of 100M at $3.75 per 1M tokens (one-time buffer top-up), refill mid-month allowed but priced at +10% on block price if outside initial commitment window
- Rollover: up to 50% of unused committed tokens can carry for up to 2 months; rollover credits expire after the second month
- SLA credits: platform-level latency/availability SLOs with crediting rules defined in the SLA appendix (available in the LOI)

Option B — Tiered Bands (flex)
- No commit; bands: 0-100M list price, 100M-500M 15% off, 500M+ 30% off for incremental consumption within the billing period
- No rollover

Option C — Pilot Dedicated for Peak Windows
- Small dedicated pool sized for weekly batch peaks (proposal priced as monthly seat + usage at a reduced per-token rate)
- Dedicated capacity can be turned on/off by schedule; unused dedicated capacity credits applied to hosted consumption at 50% value

Next steps:
- If you like Option A, we can send an LOI that includes the rate table, rollover language, and billing cadence (monthly or quarterly).
- We can include a short addendum for a one-time migration credit if you sign within 2 weeks.

Attaching the updated rate card and a one-page LOI template. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the numbers.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rate_card_v3.pdf (23 KB), LOI_template_RDW_GPV1.docx (9 KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing question: high burst and rollover credits

Sam — quick operational notes to align expectations:

- Billing cadence options: monthly invoicing (standard) or quarterly invoicing for committed customers. Quarterly invoicing requires a signed commitment addendum.
- Metering: we bill on token consumption measured at the API hop. For buffered burst pools we deduct from buffer first, then from monthly commit, then apply overage rates as defined in the LOI.
- Credits: rollover credits are applied before any overage charges and will show as line items on the invoice.

Related links: LOI in HubSpot, draft SOW template (I can attach if useful).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

All — after reviewing Option A and the attachments, GridPay wants to proceed with a short pilot under Option A (200M commit / month with a 200M buffered burst block). Two asks before we sign LOI:

1) Please include the 2-month 50% rollover language in the LOI explicitly.
2) Add a one-time migration credit of $5,000 to offset initial integration costs (we can mark as a contra-charge on the first invoice).

If you can circulate an LOI with those items this week, I will route it for approval internally.

Best regards,
Sam Levin
CTO, GridPay
